subject: arxiv:2609.26758
headline: Hosted Jev AUROC .8146 → .5806 after name–rubric swap; 0% type errors
claim_text: Swapping the rubrics behind the option names no/yes changed 32.50% of the hosted model’s answers (neutral names: 2.08% and 1.67%), lowered balanced accuracy from .7127 to .5163 and AUROC from .8146 to .5806.
task: binary workflow decisions with task-specific rubrics
limitations: Hosted model is non-deterministic; observed at one point in time.; Contrast 30.42 pts, 95% CI [27.58, 33.33].

subject: arxiv:2609.26758
headline: Test–retest floor ≤1.33% answer flips; swap = 24× the floor
claim_text: Asking the aligned arm twice (300 items × 2 name pairs), the hosted model changed at most 1.33% of answers; the name swap produced 24× that test–retest floor, and at most 36.33% of probabilities repeated bit-for-bit.
limitations: Floor measured on a subset (300 items).

subject: arxiv:2609.26758
headline: Open marker head: AUROC .9376 → .2315 (inversion), 76.92% flips
claim_text: In an open ModernBERT-large marker-readout head, the same swap changed 76.92% of answers against 6.50% behind 0/1 (difference-in-differences 70.42 pts) and inverted AUROC from .9376 to .2315.
model_version: one released checkpoint (name in unlocated harness)
limitations: This result is for an open checkpoint and must not be attributed to hosted Jev.; A mean-pooling span head flips 4.1× less often.

subject: arxiv:2609.26758
headline: Type-error rate 0% in every condition, by construction
claim_text: The type-error rate was 0% in every condition, including those where decision accuracy collapsed; the paper shows this follows from the renormalised softmax over the declared options (Lemma 1).
model: hosted model and two open heads
limitations: A 0% type-error rate is a property of the read-out, so it carries no information about decision quality.

subject: arxiv:2609.26758
headline: Random-string names return flips to the neutral regime (2–12%)
claim_text: Replacing option names with random character strings returned flip rates to the neutral-control regime in all three families (6.86%, 11.67%, 2.02%) while aligned balanced accuracy stayed within .03 of the neutral class.
limitations: Suggests neutral identifiers as a mitigation; the mitigation itself was not evaluated in deployment.

subject: arxiv:2609.26758
headline: Multi-way: neutral renaming flips 52.42%; accuracy .5637 → .2782
claim_text: On 683 multi-way questions, renaming members to neutral letters without touching descriptions changed 52.42% of answers and dropped accuracy from .5637 to .2782 (open marker head).
limitations: Pool accuracy is low (.5637); authors treat the arm as directional.

subject: arxiv:2609.26550
headline: Within 3 points of GPT-6 where the verdict can be read off the text
claim_text: On 1,500 RewardBench pairs Jev and GPT-6 Astra both scored 92.5%; on 3,000 HaluEval answers Jev scored 87.3% against 88.4%, and on final answers 94.0% against 96.7%. Pooled over 4,850 public judgments Jev ranked eighth of fifteen LLM judges, 1.7 points behind GPT-6, and it trailed by 6–15 points on difficult correctness and RM-Bench.
metric: gap to GPT-6 on pooled public judgments
limitations: Benchmark labels are imperfect; adjudication covers a disagreement-selected subset.

subject: arxiv:2609.26550
headline: 0.36% of GPT-6’s fee at 0.15 s median
claim_text: On a 120-judgment timing panel Jev’s median latency was 0.15 s (p95 0.24 s) and its fee $0.044 per 1,000 judgments, against 1.89 s and $12.182 for GPT-6 — about 277 times cheaper and 13 times faster.
limitations: Fees are estimates from reported usage at collection-time prices, not invoices.; One client location, pacing and provider load.

subject: arxiv:2609.26550
headline: Frozen cascade: +0.9 points over GPT-6 at 41% of its fee
claim_text: A two-order cascade with a threshold frozen before evaluation escalated 31% of 1,610 held-out preference pairs and beat GPT-6 alone by 0.9 points at 41% of its fee.
limitations: Held-out pairs share benchmark families with the fitting data.

subject: arxiv:2609.26550
headline: Confidence ≥ 0.9: tied with GPT-6 (94.7% vs 94.4%)
claim_text: Where Jev’s order-averaged confidence was at least 0.9, Jev and GPT-6 were nearly tied (94.7% vs 94.4% on 3,744 items); its native confidence detected errors with AUROC 0.876, 0.745 and 0.842 on RewardBench, JudgeBench and HaluEval, close to the maximum-probability values.
limitations: Native confidence is a provider-computed statistic whose implementation is not published.

subject: arxiv:2609.26532
headline: 95% success with 1.12 strong calls/task vs 88% and 4.10 (−72.7%)
claim_text: At τ = 0.5 REFLEX reached 95% success with 1.12 strong-model calls per task, against 88% and 4.10 calls for the strong-only agent — 72.7% fewer strong calls.
metric: task success; strong calls per task
limitations: Controlled benchmark shows ceiling effects for 2026 frontier models.

subject: arxiv:2609.26532
headline: BFCL / τ-style: limited edge over a cheap generative cascade
claim_text: On external BFCL tasks and 300 τ-style episodes, advantages over a cheap generative cascade with self-escalation were limited where ordinary routing was already highly accurate.
limitations: Held-out validation, not a full leaderboard with multiple trials.

subject: arxiv:2609.26532
headline: Reliability depends on action-set size and near-valid alternatives
claim_text: Controlled interventions showed that reliability depends on action-set size and on near-valid alternatives near authorisation boundaries.
task: agent decisions with varied action sets
limitations: Effects concentrate in authority and risk families.

subject: arxiv:2609.25845
headline: Macro accuracy 0.706 → 0.761 after post-training (seen families)
claim_text: Answer-supervised post-training raised equal-weight macro accuracy across four benchmarks from 0.706 to 0.761, with the gain concentrated on the two task families represented in training.
baseline: untuned Qwen3-VL-4B read through its LM head
limitations: Seen-family gains; limited transfer to unseen families.

subject: arxiv:2609.25845
headline: 8.9× vs serial, 3.4× vs no-reuse batch; 5.7 ms/question amortized
claim_text: With 32 questions per image, shared batched execution was 8.9× faster in warm amortized time than independent serial execution and 3.4× faster than batching that recomputes the prefix (5.7 ms per question; about 182 ms per 32-question batch).
baseline: independent serial; batched without prefix reuse
limitations: Amortized throughput, not independent-request latency; higher peak memory; queueing excluded.

subject: arxiv:2609.25845
headline: Typed head: no consistent gain over LM-head readout
claim_text: A matched typed-head control offered no consistent accuracy advantage over reading candidate probabilities from the backbone’s LM head.
limitations: One backbone family.

subject: arxiv:2609.24965
headline: Full semantic correctness; median 0.335 s, p95 0.442 s
claim_text: Jev matched five other configurations at complete semantic correctness on 20 Choices × 5 repetitions and had the lowest observed median latency among successful responses (0.335 s; p95 0.442 s), at about $0.000060 per successful response.
limitations: Ten cases; six configurations reach complete correctness, so the set is not discriminative.

subject: arxiv:2609.24965
headline: 7 wrong selections changed counts but not the final label
claim_text: Across three comparison models, seven wrong selections on one culture-history question changed downstream counts while preserving the correct final claim label.
locator: Abstract; §3 (correct labels can conceal wrong quantities)
limitations: Errors were made by comparison models; the point is about evaluation design, not about Jev.

subject: arxiv:2609.24574
headline: Behind best LLM on 14/15 tasks (−11.6 F1) at 44× lower cost
claim_text: Jev trailed the per-task best LLM on 14 of 15 evaluation tasks, by a median 11.6 macro-F1 points, at a median 44 times lower measured cost.
limitations: Zero-shot protocol for every model; tasks from one established suite; older corpora may overlap with training data.

subject: arxiv:2609.24574
headline: Median ECE 0.157 vs 0.066 for the best (verbalised) LLM
claim_text: Jev’s median expected calibration error over the evaluation tasks was 0.157 (95% CI [0.108, 0.233]) — lower than the verbalised-confidence error of 16 of 19 LLMs but higher than three frontier Claude models (Opus 5: 0.066).
limitations: Median intervals overlap.; Under equal-mass binning Sonnet 5 falls slightly behind Jev; Opus 5 stays ahead.

subject: arxiv:2609.24574
headline: Empathy: confident near chance; task ECE 0.538
claim_text: On the empathy task the model reported high confidence while performing near chance; the task contributes a calibration error of 0.538, and removing it lowers the median only to 0.142.
limitations: One construct; the authors do not claim the failure generalises.

subject: arxiv:2609.24574
headline: Low-confidence routing matches the LLM at ¼–½ of its cost
claim_text: Routing low-confidence items to an LLM matched or exceeded that LLM alone at roughly a quarter to half of its measured cost; items at or above 0.9 confidence reached a median accuracy of 0.815 at 0.376 coverage.
limitations: Measured on the tested tasks and LLMs only.

subject: arxiv:2609.24395
headline: PLCC vs VMAF: 0.737 (metadata) → 0.824 (+bitstream, pixel)
claim_text: Against VMAF, metadata-only JEVQA reached PLCC 0.737 (ITU-T P.1204.1: 0.733); adding bitstream data gave 0.797 and bitstream plus pixel features 0.824; a pixel-only variant failed.
baseline: ITU-T P.1204.1; models trained on the same features
limitations: Target is VMAF, not human MOS.; Trained models on the same features remain clearly ahead.

subject: arxiv:2609.24395
headline: Correlation with MOS 0.879 vs P.1204.1 0.898
claim_text: Against subjective MOS on AVT-VQDB-UHD-1, metadata-only JEVQA reached a correlation of 0.879, close to P.1204.1 (0.898); bitstream statistics did not help.
limitations: Standard models have seen part of this database.

subject: arxiv:2609.24052
headline: 499,500 narratives screened for $25.23; 195,857 fully coded
claim_text: A first-stage screen returned answers for 499,500 Texas narratives at a cost of $25.23; the second stage coded 195,857 narratives with a 27-question schema. Cost is governed by schema size rather than narrative length.
limitations: Single region and schema.

subject: arxiv:2609.24052
headline: F1 0.908 vs 2,416 human judgments; one frontier LLM +0.059
claim_text: Against 2,416 blinded human judgments the typed model reached F1 0.908; one frontier model was 0.059 higher and the other indistinguishable.
baseline: two frontier LLMs on the same records
limitations: Sampling design gives an effective sample of about 1,265.

subject: arxiv:2609.24052
headline: Recalibration on held-out labels cut calibration error ~3.3×
claim_text: Probabilities ranked well but overstated prevalence until recalibrated; recalibration fitted on half of the human labels reduced calibration error by a factor of about 3.3 (isotonic), with calibration varying by model rather than by paradigm.
limitations: Same-distribution labels; not a guarantee for new regions or schemas.

subject: arxiv:2609.24052
headline: Two-decimal probabilities set a calibration-error floor
claim_text: Because probabilities are returned on a two-decimal grid, calibration error has a resolution floor for rare variables; the paper derives a bound that applies to any model reporting probabilities on a discrete grid.
limitations: Matters most for rare positives.

subject: arxiv:2609.24052
headline: Coded fields understate narrative fidelity by 0.26 kappa
claim_text: Agreement with administrative coded fields understated fidelity to the narrative by a median of 0.26 in kappa.
baseline: coded fields vs human narrative labels
limitations: Specific to Texas CRIS fields.

subject: arxiv:2609.23986
headline: LoCoMo judge 0.777 (+11.0%); build 158 s; 0.93 s/query
claim_text: On LoCoMo, Jev-Mem reached an overall LLM-as-a-Judge score of 0.777 (+11.0% relative to the strongest baseline), built memory in 158 s (6.6× faster than the fastest competing memory system) and averaged 0.93 s per query (36.7% lower than the fastest memory baseline at 1.47 s).
metric: judge score; build time; query latency
limitations: Gains belong to the whole system; each number has a different baseline; LLM-judge metric.

subject: arxiv:2609.23959
headline: JevLite ensemble AUROC .974, ECE .052; no false alarms
claim_text: A three-seed JevLite ensemble reached AUROC .974 with calibration error .052 on 577 turn-level decisions, non-inferior to an LLM judge (MiniMax-M3) at a pre-registered .02 margin, with no false alarms on legitimate calls and decisions 1.14 turns earlier.
limitations: Recipe selection had test-set exposure.; All callers synthetic.; Fine-tuned ModernBERT not significantly worse.

subject: arxiv:2609.23959
headline: 64.5 ms/decision; 4.9× faster than same backbone generating
claim_text: JevLite took 64.5 ms per decision on one consumer GPU, 4.9× lower than the same backbone fine-tuned to generate its answer.
baseline: same Qwen3-4B backbone fine-tuned to generate
limitations: Single-model latency; the three-model ensemble quality is a different scope.

subject: arxiv:2609.23886
headline: 30.9 ms per decision on one laptop GPU; 32 decisions/s
claim_text: this-that-model-1.0 decided in 30.9 ms end to end on one laptop GPU and sustained 32 decisions per second, generating no output tokens.
limitations: Local timing; not comparable to hosted end-to-end latency that includes the network.

subject: arxiv:2609.23886
headline: 68 questions: 0.941 (Brier .042) vs Jev 0.765 (.133); gap = 12 items
claim_text: On a third party’s recorded cohort of 68 questions over 17 states, this-that-model scored 0.941 accuracy (Brier 0.042) against Jev’s 0.765 (0.133); the authors note the 18-point gap rests on 12 questions.
baseline: hosted Jev on the same items
limitations: Small cohort; wording chosen by the third party.

subject: arxiv:2609.23886
headline: 2,250 questions: 0.844 vs Jev 0.803 — on the open model’s training shapes
claim_text: On the 2,250-question subset of the released benchmark every hosted system answered, Jev scored 0.803 against this-that-model’s 0.844 — a comparison the authors call not clean because their model was trained on those question shapes (training moved it from 0.409 to 0.844).
limitations: Training-distribution advantage for the open model.

subject: arxiv:2609.23886
headline: $0.000217 electricity per suite pass vs $10.636 for a hosted model
claim_text: One pass of the 42-family internal suite cost $0.000217 of electricity (80 W at $0.30/kWh) against $10.636 and 155.2 minutes for the most accurate hosted model measured.
limitations: Electricity-only marginal cost excludes hardware, operations and margin; not an API price.; Internal suite is not released.

subject: arxiv:2609.22753
headline: Median decision latency −22.7% to −64.5% vs the fastest LLM
claim_text: Across 33 test conditions on 8,280 verified requests, Jev reduced median decision latency by 22.7–64.5% relative to the fastest hosted LLM, and its latency barely moved with input size, contract width or catalog size.
limitations: Provider, region and time-window specific.

subject: arxiv:2609.22753
headline: Fees per correct decision −60% to −81% on four-field contracts
claim_text: On four-field contracts, Jev’s API fees per correct decision were 59.7–80.9% lower than the hosted LLMs’ at a cost of a few exact-match points; wide contracts marked the limit of the substitution.
limitations: Caching-disabled conditions only for the latency figure.

subject: arxiv:2609.22753
headline: With caching, latencies converge: the gain is in fresh decisions
claim_text: Caching repeated descriptions gave the interpreters nearly the same latency, so Jev’s advantage lies in fresh decisions.
limitations: Cache policy specific to the tested service.

subject: arxiv:2609.25498
headline: Self-reported 81.65% on public JevBench items at 7.08 ms
claim_text: The authors report 81.65% calibrated accuracy and 100% format compliance on the 231 public JevBench items, with a 7.08 ms median latency.
limitations: Self-reported; leaderboard claim relies on a community submission.

subject: arxiv:2609.25498
headline: “0% bypass” with a 95% interval up to 27.8%
claim_text: The reported 0.0% empirical prompt-injection bypass carries a 95% Wilson interval of 0.0–27.8%, which implies a very small number of evaluated vectors.
limitations: Not a security guarantee.

subject: src:typesafe-launch
headline: No type errors by construction; plotted 0% is analytical
claim_text: TypeSafe states that Jev never makes type errors because possible outputs are defined in advance, and that its plotted 0% is analytical rather than empirical.
limitations: Schema conformance only; says nothing about semantic correctness.

subject: src:typesafe-launch
headline: $0.042 / M input tokens; 70–500 ms end to end (vendor)
claim_text: Launch materials report input pricing of $0.042 per million tokens with free output and an end-to-end response time of 70–500 ms, measured from the vendor’s West Coast laptops.
limitations: Vendor notes it cannot prove the price is not subsidised.; Region- and load-dependent.

subject: src:typesafe-launch
headline: 193.6× faster, 444.6× cheaper on vendor workflow evals
claim_text: The “193.6× faster, 444.6× cheaper” headline comes from the vendor’s workflow evaluations, whose reference answers average two external frontier models; the vendor expects these to be on the higher end of real-world gains and notes the workflows were written by its capabilities team.
limitations: Reference answers are model outputs, not ground truth.; Possible selection bias acknowledged by the vendor.

subject: src:typesafe-docs-confidence
headline: Confidence = a statistic of the returned distribution
claim_text: Choice and Score answers return a probability for every option or level and a confidence value computed from that distribution; Noul answers return only the probability of yes. The documentation calls confidence a convenient statistic and recommends thresholds tested on the user’s own data.
limitations: The exact statistic is not specified in the prose; the interactive demo’s formula is labelled as how the demo computes it.

subject: src:typesafe-docs-system-one
headline: Calibration is a group property, not a per-answer guarantee
claim_text: The vendor states that calibration is measured across groups of predictions and does not guarantee that an individual answer is correct.

subject: src:typesafe-docs-models
headline: Text-only input; English is the primary training language
claim_text: jev-1.13.0 accepts text only (a string, JSON object or array of text values); images, audio and video must be pre-processed into text or structured fields. English is the primary training language.
limitations: Visual Jev and JEVQA do not change this: one is an independent model, the other feeds text features.

subject: src:typesafe-docs-jaggedness
headline: Vendor-listed failure modes for jev-1.13
claim_text: The vendor’s jev-1.13 “jaggedness” page lists known failure modes: literal reading, math and numbers (including counting and numeric representations), date and time comparison, indirection, large state full of irrelevant detail, adversarial content, contradictory instructions and criteria, Choice option order (a lean toward the first option) and generation.
limitations: A boundary statement by the vendor, not a neutral evaluation.

subject: src:typesafe-docs-models
headline: Aliases point to jev-1.13.0; pin versions when tuning thresholds
claim_text: Aliases jev-latest and jev-preview both pointed to jev-1.13.0 at the time of review; the vendor advises pinning the versioned ID when thresholds were tuned to a specific version.

subject: src:typesafe-docs-models
headline: Same weights for all accounts; architecture undisclosed
claim_text: Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data; it is trained with RLCD and the same weights serve every account. Architecture and training data are not documented.

subject: gh:jujumilk3/jev-calibration-audit
headline: Abstain removed: acc 0.95 → 0; Noul vs Choice differ by 0.125
claim_text: Seven API-only experiments (about 7,000 calls) report that removing the abstain option drove accuracy on unanswerable items from 0.950 to 0.000 at 0.79 confidence, that a Noul and a two-option Choice over the same question differed by 0.125 on average, that 50 identical requests gave 15 distinct answers, and that option order produced no argmax flips in 400 trials.
limitations: Community report; not peer-reviewed.

subject: gh:jourdanlabs/assay-001
headline: ECE 0.0204 (CLINC150) vs 0.0936 (Banking77); 0 type errors
claim_text: A pre-registered audit reports Jev’s chosen-option probabilities as calibrated on CLINC150 (ECE 0.0204) but systematically overconfident on Banking77 (ECE 0.0936), with zero type errors across 8,576 responses.
limitations: Community report; protocol frozen before queries, per the README.

subject: gh:marcosmartinez/jev-acento
headline: Spanish state: −3.0 to −6.4 accuracy points on 4 datasets
claim_text: With English instructions and a Spanish state, jev-1.13.0 lost 3.0–6.4 accuracy points on all four datasets (XNLI, PAWS-X, MASSIVE, Belebele) across 3,200 paired items and 19,200 calls; ECE roughly doubled on the two hardest tasks.
limitations: Community report; pre-registered, per the README.

subject: gh:scienthoon/jev-ood-calibration
headline: Unknowable-rule task: temperature ≈3.4 needed; 0.01 quantisation
claim_text: On a rule-based task whose label is not recoverable from the text, the chosen level averaged 0.74 probability and a temperature of about 3.4 was needed to make probabilities honest; the returned probabilities were quantised to 0.01 and the gateway exposed no model version.
limitations: Unpinned model alias; post-hoc temperature diagnostic.

subject: gh:jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey
headline: Noul vs Choice framing reverses the comparison with GPT-4.1
claim_text: Playing 300 survey respondents, jev-1.13.0 asked through Noul led GPT-4.1 on all six distribution measures, but asked through a two-option Choice it trailed on the distribution gap (0.1985 vs 0.1789): the primitive changes the conclusion.
limitations: “Survey” here means a questionnaire study, not a literature review.; Community report.

subject: gh:nokia-applied-research/anyjev
headline: Frozen Qwen3-8B: order flips 0.230 → 0.073; auto-decidable 7.7% → 52%
claim_text: For a frozen Qwen3-8B on BANKING77 (20-way, 300 items), label-free permutation calibration reduced answer flips under option reversal from 0.230 to 0.073 and ECE from 0.240 to 0.184; with 100–500 labels ECE fell to 0.095 and the share decidable at ≤5% error rose from 7.7% to 52.0%.
limitations: Point estimate at n=300; wide interval per README.

subject: gh:githubnext/localjev
headline: Wire-compatible, not a logit read: probabilities are generated
claim_text: LocalJev returns Jev-shaped responses by asking a model for JSON probabilities, validating, retrying and normalising them; its README states this is wire-compatible but not mathematically equivalent to a logit read.

subject: gh:theoleecj/semif
headline: Reproduces the interface pattern, not Jev’s model or training
claim_text: SemIf (formerly OpenJev) reproduces the interface pattern with a frozen open model’s option-token probabilities and states that it does not reproduce Jev’s undisclosed model or training.

subject: gh:jaredpalmer/kev
headline: Architecture follows third-party speculation, not a disclosure
claim_text: Kev states that it follows an architecture described in a third-party blog post about Jev; that description is community speculation, not a disclosure by TypeSafe.

subject: arxiv:2609.27678
headline: $0.000228 and 1.24 s per contract — lowest of ten models
claim_text: On the 123-contract baseline Jev had the lowest cost and median response time of the ten configurations: $0.000228 per contract and 1.24 s (P95 1.59 s), against $0.001353 and 1.60 s for Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and $0.000931 and 1.74 s for GPT-5.6 Luna.
limitations: Costs are token usage times public prices; latency includes network and provider infrastructure.; One client; providers and collection times differ.

subject: arxiv:2609.27678
headline: Accuracy 77.38% vs 78.96–83.21% for hosted LLMs
claim_text: Baseline accuracy was 77.38% [75.99, 78.81] for Jev against 78.96–83.21% for the seven hosted language models; Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite gained 5.16 points (paired 95% interval 3.49–6.98) at about six times the cost, while the gain for GPT-5.6 Luna was not established.
limitations: Invalid responses count as incorrect for every model.; The held-out split does not establish absence from training data.

subject: arxiv:2609.27678
headline: 23/30 anchors correct in all 12 responses; 5 consistently wrong
claim_text: On 30 fixed anchors answered twelve times each, Jev kept 23 correct in every response (Claude Sonnet 5: 24; Claude Haiku 4.5: 19). Five of Jev’s anchors received the same wrong label every time, so agreement across repeats overstated correctness.
metric: anchors correct in all twelve responses
limitations: The Sonnet–Jev difference is one target, with an interval spanning zero.; Jev’s output-order condition changes question-key order only.

subject: arxiv:2609.27607
headline: Kendall τ 0.573 / 0.398 with expert error counts; beats open NLI
claim_text: A one-question Jev configuration reached Kendall τ 0.573 on RadEvalX and 0.398 on RadEvalExpert with expert total-error counts, exceeding an open NLI judge with the same statements and aggregation; RadMatch on a local 27B model was stronger on clinically significant errors (0.491 vs 0.346 on RadEvalX).
limitations: Agreement with reference text, not with the image.; Local baselines use a substituted 27B backend.

subject: arxiv:2609.27607
headline: Under $0.03 per 100 report pairs (judgment calls only)
claim_text: One support question per statement kept expert agreement close to the seven-question design with 43–45% fewer input tokens; the judgment calls cost about $0.000226–0.000258 per report pair, under three cents per hundred pairs, excluding local statement extraction.
metric: judgment API cost per report pair
limitations: Priced from token counts at the list price; local decomposition cost excluded.

subject: arxiv:2609.27607
headline: Raw ECE 0.12; isotonic recalibration → 0.008 on holdout
claim_text: Raw sentence-level probabilities had ECE 0.1192 on the ReXErr test set (open NLI: 0.1045); isotonic calibration fitted on half of the studies lowered Jev’s ECE on the other half from 0.1235 to 0.0077.
limitations: Calibration fitted and tested on halves of the same benchmark.; Measured on the multi-question configuration’s support outputs.

subject: arxiv:2609.27535
headline: 1.7% flagship anchors cut effect error 41%; decision gain 0.27 → 0.39
claim_text: Flagship anchors covering 1.7% of Epstein states lowered effect MAE from 0.0305 to 0.0180 (paired improvement 0.0125, 95% interval 0.0064–0.0167); on 37 held-out SocSci210 experiments, 0.5–1.5% anchor coverage raised captured decision gain from 0.268 to 0.386.
limitations: Preregistered policy-value and heterogeneity primaries were not shown.; Corrections can import the flagship’s errors.

subject: arxiv:2609.27535
headline: Passes content gates in 15/15 new countries; fails intervention gates
claim_text: The Jev kernel passed the content-fidelity gates in all 15 new countries of a 16-country study but failed both intervention-sensitivity gates, which GPT-6 Astra passed.
limitations: Models read English in all countries; this does not test multilingual inference.

subject: arxiv:2609.27535
headline: $0.0227 per 1,000 predictions; median 213 ms
claim_text: Fresh Jev predictions cost $0.0227 per thousand with median latency 213 ms (p95 304 ms); GPT-6 Astra cost about 312–455 times as much per prediction, and a million agents executed 20 tabulated steps in 0.90 s on a laptop.
limitations: Flagship costs are subscription-billed usage converted at list prices.; Tabulated execution time excludes fresh inference.

subject: arxiv:2609.27535
headline: Shared discrepancy: 93% / 96% coverage vs 29% / 36% sampling-only
claim_text: Propagating a fitted human–model discrepancy gave retrospective coverage of 0.93 and 0.96 at nominal 0.80 and 0.90 on 37 unseen studies, against 0.29 and 0.36 from human sampling uncertainty alone.
limitations: Retrospective; fitted on studies selected for reliable contrasts.

subject: arxiv:2609.27331
headline: 4/4 full-game wins incl. two vs Lv7 with GPT-6 plans; Jev-only never expanded
claim_text: With GPT-6 plans, the controller won all four completed non-cheating full games, including two against Lv7; the earlier Jev-only controller reached its 20-minute limit against Lv2 without ever expanding.
limitations: The two controllers also differ in candidate descriptions and execution handling.; Opponents are not matched between controllers.

subject: arxiv:2609.27331
headline: Enemy elimination 16.5% → 37.7%; wins 3 → 7 of 105
claim_text: Across 35 SMAC-Hard maps with three episodes each, the combined system raised mean enemy elimination from 16.50% to 37.69% and wins from 3 to 7 out of 105.
limitations: One shared plan per map; the three episodes are not independent planner samples.

subject: arxiv:2609.27331
headline: Jev 0.422 s median; $0.15 of $3.71 per game
claim_text: Median Jev response time was 0.422 s (P95 0.531 s) in full games against 27.60 s for GPT-6 planning calls; of USD 3.71 estimated model cost per game, Jev accounted for USD 0.15 and planning for 96%.
limitations: Costs are standard-API-equivalent estimates from recorded usage.; Real-time games overlap inference with play.

subject: arxiv:2609.26550
headline: Pre-specified live test: matched GPT-6 exactly, 74% escalated
claim_text: In a pre-specified live test on 570 held-out pairs from two new correctness workloads, where Jev alone trailed GPT-6 by 14 points, the cascade with thresholds chosen on 100 local labels per workload matched GPT-6’s accuracy exactly (88.2% and 94.7%), escalating 74% of pairs and costing 75.5% of GPT-6’s fee.
limitations: Two correctness workloads; savings shrink when Jev trails the fallback.

subject: arxiv:2609.22753
headline: Live admission: 0.91–0.95 exact and on time where LLMs fall below 0.1
claim_text: On a live admission path with modeled execution, Jev kept 0.91–0.95 of requests exact and on time at loads where the hosted LLMs fell below 0.1.
metric: share of requests exact and on time
limitations: Execution is modeled on the admission path.

subject: arxiv:2609.23136
headline: Meets the 1 s RIC budget on 99.8% of calls (LLMs: 17.9%, 0%)
claim_text: Median interpretation took 0.286–2.35 s across interpreters against under 25 ms for A1 and E2 transfer; Jev-1.13.0 met the 1 s near-real-time budget on 99.8% of calls (0.286 s median, 0.391 s p95 on the real path), while two hosted LLMs met it on 17.9% and 0%.
metric: calls meeting the 1 s near-RT budget
limitations: Hosted latency from one client site.

subject: arxiv:2609.23136
headline: Radio conditions outweigh the interpreter; no LLM gain over Jev
claim_text: In closed-loop simulation, ideal enforcement moved the affected-class SLA violation by 3.96 points in the requested direction while radio conditions moved it more; no hosted LLM showed a resolved gain over Jev-1.13.0, and per-second direct control gave no resolved SLA reduction over a numerical xApp.
limitations: Simulated radio network.

subject: arxiv:2609.23136
headline: Under load, slow interpreters saturate — a small local JSON model keeps up too
claim_text: At 2 intents per second two interpreters, the open AnyJev-L0 and the hosted Qwen3.8-Flash, saturated their queues, while Jev-1.13.0 and the other five interpreters, including a small self-hosted JSON-generating reference model, stayed below the stationarity boundary.
limitations: Synthetic arrival process.

subject: arxiv:2609.28587
headline: Range refinement: 83.4% within 5% vs 80.5% direct choice
claim_text: On 256 arithmetic expressions, ten-way NumericJev placed 83.40% of outputs within 5% relative error against 80.47% for direct choice from a list containing the answer, and lowered range-normalised MAE from 5.18% to 1.60–1.84%; with the answer supplied, direct choice reached 97.27%.
limitations: A 16-point gap to the answer-supplied control remains: the model still has to compute.; Arithmetic benchmark built by the authors.

subject: arxiv:2609.28613
headline: Injection shifts probabilities (+0.043) but rarely selects the target (1.8%)
claim_text: Original injected content increased the mean attacker-target probability by 0.043 but selected the attacker’s target in 9 of 510 cases (1.8%); override markers reduced the effect.
task: Prompt injection on typed tool selection
limitations: Three-way action space; larger action sets not established.; Selection, not executed harm.

subject: arxiv:2609.28613
headline: Score feedback doubles attacker probability; success 1.8% → 3.5%
claim_text: With 24 score-guided proposals, the mean best attacker-target probability doubled from 0.043 to 0.084 and validated success on fresh calls rose from 1.8% to 3.5%; successes concentrated where the clean decision margin was small.
limitations: Exploratory link to decision margins.; Requires access to returned probabilities.

subject: arxiv:2609.28919
headline: Emulated router saves 13–21% of coding-agent spend
claim_text: In an emulated 10,000-seat enterprise, routing turns with Jev’s prompt labels recovered 13–21% of model spend; a Jev call took about 250 ms at the median over the public internet.
limitations: Emulation over synthetic conversations; no measured deployment outcome.; User pauses move the saving as much as the classifier does.

subject: arxiv:2609.28940
headline: One run each: 5 min faster, different severities — not a controlled test
claim_text: In a single run per arm on one target, the Jev-enabled harness finished 5 min 19 s faster (26 m 53 s vs 32 m 12 s) and shifted severity grading (8 High vs 3, 3 Critical vs 4); the author treats this as motivation, not evidence.
limitations: One run per arm; differences may come from LLM stochasticity.

subject: arxiv:2609.29283
headline: Typed readout and generation gain equally after adaptation
claim_text: After 64-shot adaptation, generation and direct typed readout from the same checkpoint rose together on Pets (56.36% → 91.63% for both paths), so the improvement came from adaptation, not from the decision interface; a DINOv2 probe still reached 95.67%.
limitations: Open 2B/4B checkpoints only.

subject: arxiv:2609.29429
headline: Zero-shot failure detection: median AUROC 0.886 at 1/63 of judge cost
claim_text: A single generic yes/no question reached a median AUROC of 0.886 over the 31 benchmarks that admit it, above supervised TF-IDF and length baselines on 25, and a pass over 19 judge-scored benchmarks cost $0.30, about 63 times less than their judges.
limitations: Supplying the defining reference matters more than added context (e.g. PrivacyLens 0.79 → 0.95).

subject: arxiv:2609.29429
headline: Ranks well, thresholds badly: median ECE 0.168 vs null 0.074
claim_text: Jev’s probabilities ranked failures well but did not transfer as thresholds: median ECE was 0.168 against a null of 0.074, because the mean probability missed each benchmark’s base rate; a threshold fitted on ten labelled items recovered most of the F1.
limitations: Base rates differ by benchmark.

subject: arxiv:2609.29769
headline: Parity on most rubric criteria at 1/16–1/325 of the cost
claim_text: Against per-criterion LLM judges, Jev differed significantly in only 8 of 27 paired accuracy comparisons and reached parity in 8 more; the LLM judges cost 16 to 325 times as much and took 28 to 350 times as long.
limitations: Behind on ordinal criteria; flash-tier comparators.

subject: arxiv:2609.29769
headline: Judges share Jev’s confident errors (96%); cascades gain ≤2.7 points
claim_text: On Jev’s most confident errors, 96.0% of LLM verdicts repeated its answer against 50.3% expected under independence, and cascades beat the best single judge by at most 2.7 points even with oracle thresholds.
metric: LLM agreement with Jev’s most confident errors
limitations: Errors may reflect label conventions rather than model faults.

subject: arxiv:2609.30186
headline: AndroidWorld 79% (vs 84% step-wise) at 73% lower API cost
claim_text: On the full AndroidWorld suite, Jev-Mobile reached 0.79 task success against 0.78 for SeeAct-V and 0.84 for a step-wise VLM, while cutting mean successful-trajectory time from 197.21 to 132.67 s and API cost from $0.274 to $0.073 against the step-wise agent.
limitations: Timing and cost on successful trajectories only.; The executor was not ablated against other choice models.

subject: arxiv:2609.30216
headline: Ecosystem: judgment 77%, scoring 52%, action selection 31% of projects
claim_text: Across 2,170 public repositories, attribute judgment appeared in 77% of projects, scoring or ranking in 52% and action selection in 31%; Choice appeared in 81.0%, Noul in 72.2% and Score in 45.4%, and 69.7% of projects with an identified purpose used Jev for two or more purposes.
metric: share of projects using attribute judgment
limitations: LLM-assisted labelling; snapshot of 22 September 2026.

subject: arxiv:2609.30243
headline: Natural context flips 61% of correct decisions (vs 2% neutral)
claim_text: Within 64 accepted target evaluations, optimised natural context redirected 312 of 508 initially correct decisions (61.4%, Wilson 57.1–65.5%), 229 of them with at least 0.7 probability on the wrong target; one target-aware addition flipped 16.9% against 2.2% for a neutral one.
limitations: Requires probability feedback and a query budget.

subject: arxiv:2609.30454
headline: Confidence = chance-normalised max probability; pooled ECE 0.034
claim_text: The vendor’s confidence field matched a chance-normalised maximum probability for 97.9% of 6,020 records; read that way, pooled ECE was 0.034 and AUROC 0.820 for separating correct from incorrect answers, with per-task ECE from 0.033 to 0.193.
limitations: Pooling flatters calibration; per-task values matter.

subject: arxiv:2609.30454
headline: Option rotation changes 37% of answers; aggregate accuracy hides it
claim_text: Under four cyclic rotations of the answer options, 37.4% of WMDP-Cyber items received different answers against 9.2% across four identical calls, leaving 28.2 points attributable to option order (WMDP-Bio: 10.6% vs 2.4%); aggregate accuracy moved by under 1.3 points.
metric: items with changed answers across rotations
limitations: Multiple-choice items with 2–10 options.

subject: arxiv:2609.30706
headline: Learned “when to ask” policy ≈ oracle (AUC 0.80 vs 0.80)
claim_text: A value-of-information head trained alongside the decision head matched an oracle asking policy closely (accuracy–questions AUC 0.799–0.800 vs 0.800–0.803) and chose the same slot to ask about in 88–92% of cases.
limitations: Synthetic dialogues; the head does not learn that value vanishes as certainty grows out of distribution.

subject: arxiv:2609.30922
headline: Jev-routed LoRA composition: +0.2 to +1.2 points
claim_text: Choosing two LoRA experts with Jev and composing them orthogonally beat the strongest external baseline by 1.13, 1.19 and 0.21 macro points at 1.7B, 4B and 8B.
metric: macro accuracy gain over best baseline
limitations: Small margins; routing and composition effects are partly separated in an ablation.

subject: arxiv:2609.31142
headline: An appended opinion flips 12% and drains 38% of confident answers below the gate
claim_text: An observer’s opinion appended to the state flipped 12.1% [8.5, 15.5] of decisions, statistically tied with the strongest injected command (10.1%), and pushed 38.0% of confident Choice and Score answers below a 0.8 confidence gate against 0.5% under an identical re-run.
limitations: Flips measured against the model’s own clean answers.

subject: arxiv:2609.31142
headline: Identical re-run changes the Score value on 38.5% of Score questions
claim_text: Sending an identical request twice changed the returned Score value for 38.5% of Score questions; the identical re-run flip rate over all 812 questions was 1.0%.
metric: Score questions with a changed value on re-run
limitations: Score values may move between levels without changing the most likely level.

subject: arxiv:2609.33209
headline: P(X) + P(not X) misses 1 by 0.064 (open LLM readout: 0.293)
claim_text: On 480 negation pairs, Jev’s probabilities for “the label is X” and “the label is not X” missed summing to one by 0.064 on average (95% CI 0.055–0.072), against 0.293 for Qwen3.8-27B’s first-token readout and 0.122 for its verbalised probabilities.
limitations: Two English domains; one negation wording.

subject: arxiv:2609.33209
headline: Three single-label probabilities sum to 1.14
claim_text: Jev over-endorsed statements about single labels: its three single-label probabilities summed to 1.14 on average, and its violations were about five times its repeat noise, concentrating where its answer was uncertain.
limitations: Coherence checks need no labels but cannot say which answer is right.

subject: arxiv:2609.33401
headline: Safe automation coverage: 7.6% (symmetric) → 47% (separate thresholds)
claim_text: Under a fixed symmetric review policy, Jev could automate only 7.63% of R-Judge inputs within the miss and blocking limits; choosing block and allow thresholds separately raised coverage to 47.03%, entirely through additional blocks.
limitations: Coverage depends on error limits set by the authors.

subject: arxiv:2609.33401
headline: Open Jev-like models: Laya AUROC 0.53 vs Jev 0.96 on R-Judge
claim_text: On shared R-Judge inputs, Laya’s AUROC was 0.533 against Jev’s 0.961 and its Brier score 0.272 against 0.103 — worse than a constant base-rate forecast; Bespoke Nimble led WAInjectBench yet flagged 92.8% of benign R-Judge interactions as unsafe.
limitations: Open checkpoints run as shipped, without task adaptation.

subject: arxiv:2609.33538
headline: Rescoring: WER 7.5% vs 7.8% for 7B LLMs, no GPU needed
claim_text: On 978 held-out sentences, Jev rescoring reached 7.46% word error against 7.80% for OPT-6.7b and 7.75% for Qwen2.5-7B (decoder alone 8.1%), at $0.07 per thousand sentences; end-to-end latency was 262 ms over the internet against 27 ms for a local 7B model.
limitations: One participant; one decoder.

subject: arxiv:2609.33671
headline: Adapted open guard: AUC 0.83 → 0.997, with an OOD “alignment tax”
claim_text: Boundary adaptation raised Laya-322M from ROC-AUC 0.827 zero-shot to 0.997 on DUCS-Bench with 0.42% benign false positives, while out-of-distribution accuracy on SafetyBench-ZH fell from 60.33% to 56.81% before replay recovered it to 64–65%.
limitations: In-house benchmark; NPU-specific latency.

subject: arxiv:2609.33689
headline: Hosted Jev never meets 100 ms near-RT deadlines (warm p50 281 ms)
claim_text: Jev’s median latency from the testbed was network-bound (TCP connection alone 199 ms; warm p50 281 ms, cold 726 ms) and never reached the 100 ms class, while local specialists stayed within about 30 ms at p99; a co-located decoding LLM made 12–56% of local decisions miss 100 ms.
limitations: One site and network path.

subject: arxiv:2609.33689
headline: Zero-shot Jev 0.67 on rule-defined classes vs 0.90–0.92 for specialists
claim_text: On rule-defined known decision classes, zero-shot Jev reached 0.67 accuracy against 0.92 for a fine-tuned encoder and 0.90 for fine-tuned Laya, yet it answered at least 0.98 on six of eight new counterfactual question templates and gained when the rule was stated (anomaly severity 0.347 → 0.880).
limitations: Specialists answer only the questions they were trained on.

subject: arxiv:2609.33843
headline: Open Laya checkpoint under-confident (gap −0.214); one temperature fixes it
claim_text: The shipped Laya checkpoint reproduced its card accuracy (0.767 vs 0.766) but was uniformly under-confident — signed confidence–accuracy gap −0.214 with every occupied bin’s accuracy above its confidence — and a single temperature of 0.469 cut held-out ECE from 0.204 to 0.037.
limitations: Gold labels are a synthetic teacher’s answers.

subject: arxiv:2609.33874
headline: Local likelihood readout 85.1% vs Jev 89.1% on MMLU
claim_text: On the 14,042-question MMLU test set, the best local candidate-likelihood configuration reached 85.09% at 2.21 requests/s, 3.97 points below the author’s evaluation of Jev 1.13 (89.06% at 2.86 requests/s).
limitations: Jev number from a separate manual run.

subject: arxiv:2609.33971
headline: Staged decisions disagree with direct ones; Jev loses 22.9 points on CLINC150
claim_text: Across 72,000 classification questions, mean category-level total variation between direct and staged predictions was 0.219–0.349 for Jev and 0.424–0.689 for Laya; staging cut Jev’s CLINC150 accuracy by 22.9 points [−24.9, −20.9] and raised Laya’s by 21.3.
limitations: Hierarchies fixed by the authors.

subject: arxiv:2609.34024
headline: Medicine: parity on abstracts, −22 points on diagnostic cases
claim_text: Jev’s accuracy matched GPT-6 Sol with medium reasoning on PubMedQA (78.4% vs 78.2%) but was lower on MetaMedQA (74.8% vs 82.7%) and much lower on DiagnosisArena-MCQ (59.8% vs 82.4%) and the NEJM Case Challenges (61.8% vs 82.4%).
limitations: Text-only inputs; examination-style items.

subject: arxiv:2609.34024
headline: Picks “I don’t know” on 10.5% of unanswerable questions
claim_text: Of 162 questions whose correct answer was “I don’t know or cannot answer”, Jev chose that option for 10.5% (GPT-6 Sol 8.6%); on MetaMedQA its probabilities were better calibrated than GPT-6 Sol’s (ECE 0.063 vs 0.146).
limitations: Unanswerable items come from one benchmark.

subject: arxiv:2609.34180
headline: Same evidence, different readout: +18 AP on one dataset, none on the other
claim_text: With the same caption evidence, Jev Noul reached 75.99% AP on XD-Violence against 57.81% for the stronger Qwen ordinal-likelihood readout (+18.18 points, 95% interval 5.53–31.50); on UCF-Crime the ordinal readout instead had higher AUC (65.95% vs 52.26%).
limitations: Few positives; exploratory.

subject: arxiv:2609.34227
headline: One Jev selection call ≈ LLM-extraction memory at 1/3,061 the write cost
claim_text: At a tight budget on LoCoMo, raw turns selected by a single Jev call were non-inferior to an LLM-extraction memory (one-sided 95% bound −3.0 points against a −5-point margin) at 3,061 times lower write cost, and non-inferior to a gpt-4o-mini listwise reranker at about a third of its latency.
limitations: Human grading narrows the margin.; Gain depends on the answer budget.

subject: arxiv:2609.34736
headline: Typed-question features route LLMs: 72.1% vs 69.2% best single model
claim_text: Routing on JEV’s probability answers to interpretable questions reached 72.08% average accuracy on LLMRouterBench against 69.23% for the strongest single model, and a JEV-based semantic state outperformed a Laya-based one.
limitations: One benchmark; split differs from published routers.

subject: arxiv:2609.34862
headline: Trace security: F1 77.8 vs 74.1 for the best LLM judge
claim_text: Across four trace-security benchmarks (5,219 trajectories), JEV’s benchmark-averaged positive-class F1 was 77.8 against 74.1 for GLM-5.2, with a 2.7-point paired advantage [0.5, 4.8]; median latency 0.99 s and about $0.000195 per valid judgment.
limitations: Leads on two of four datasets; GLM more precise overall.

subject: arxiv:2609.34963
headline: CWE triage: Top-1 0.46 vs 0.50 (frontier) at 1/56 of the cost
claim_text: On 50-way CWE classification, Jev reached Top-1 0.458 (GPT-5.6-Sol 0.495; best open model 0.335) and Top-5 0.836, at $0.283 against $15.83 and a 0.244 s against 1.531 s median latency; Jev-guided repair raised the security pass rate to 70.7% against 66.1% for LLM-guided repair.
limitations: Pass rate measured by the benchmark’s own detector.

subject: arxiv:2609.34969
headline: Navigation: 27% SR at 0.65 s/step; components, not just Jev, carry the gain
claim_text: On R2R-CE, NavJev reached 27.0% SR and 22.4% SPL at 0.65 s per step (Open-Nav with GPT-4o: 19.0% SR at 27.0 s); in the ablation, the compression and memory components raised SR from 19.0% to 27.0% with Jev fixed.
limitations: 100-episode ablation split.

subject: arxiv:2609.35286
headline: Jev’s argument scores move with the stated source
claim_text: In a separately registered supplement of 288 ratings, Jev’s scores of the same German and Swiss policy arguments varied with the stated source, with five source–argument interactions above the 0.05 reference adopted for the chat models.
limitations: Different rubric from the chat models; interrupted collection.

subject: arxiv:2609.35293
headline: SemEval ABSA: best regression error with 488 fitted coefficients
claim_text: Without generating text or tuning a backbone, the Jev-based system reached 1.0645 RMSE on ten-corpus valence–arousal regression, the lowest aggregate of any SemEval-2026 participant, and supervised calibration of its scores roughly halved the raw error.
limitations: Calibration fits benchmark labels.

subject: arxiv:2609.35342
headline: Known-probability test: Noul 0.92, Score 0.89, Choice 0.76
claim_text: Against exactly known probabilities, Jev’s Noul and Score answers reached soft accuracy 0.918 and 0.886 but its Choice answers only 0.764 (SemIf 0.629); modelling an implicit “unknown” share raised Choice to 0.931.
limitations: Synthetic propositions.

subject: arxiv:2609.35865
headline: Open recipe holds up; extra terms buy robustness, not accuracy
claim_text: Properly reproduced, the released Nimble recipe stayed the most accurate and best-calibrated run (85.2%, ECE 5.4%); PACT reached 84.6% but cut answer flips under relabelling from 13.8% to 9.8% and Score MAE from 0.311 to 0.232.
limitations: Three seeds; one dataset.

subject: arxiv:2609.36059
headline: Memory agent: LoCoMo 91.7% with Jev judging evidence (AUC 0.94)
claim_text: With raw records and Jev judging retrieved evidence, Mnemon reached 91.7% on LoCoMo and 83.8% on LongMemEval-S from under 4k tokens per question; on the same records Jev separated gold evidence with AUC 0.942 against 0.900 and 0.853 for two LLMs, 3–11 times faster.
limitations: Benchmarks were not held out during development.

subject: arxiv:2609.36115
headline: Single-token LLM classifier: 85.5% at 0.53 s, flat across label spaces
claim_text: A fine-tuned single-token generative classifier reached 85.5% on an intent-routing benchmark, within 2 points of the strongest frontier models, at 0.53 s median and 0.63 s p95, with medians within 3 ms of each other across very different label spaces.
limitations: Production data not released.

subject: arxiv:2609.36116
headline: Native typed-decision head: 86.2% vs Jev 85.0% on JevBench
claim_text: On JevBench, Dyad with reasoning reached 86.18% overall accuracy against Jev’s 85.01%, with the largest advantage on the hard subset; on ALFWorld, adding the native decision head gave up to 5.89 points.
limitations: Reasoning enabled for Dyad; code not yet released.

subject: arxiv:2609.36154
headline: Sensor activity recognition from text: macro-F1 ≤ 0.12
claim_text: From textual descriptions of accelerometer windows, Jev’s best representation reached macro-F1 of only 0.038, 0.118 and 0.089 on WISDM, UCI341 and PAMAP2, far below supervised HAR models, and its probabilities were not reliably calibrated.
limitations: Interface (rendering) is part of the result.

subject: arxiv:2609.36399
headline: Persona shifts reproduce 87% (English) vs 62% (Arabic) of a human difference
claim_text: Switching personas from American to Saudi moved Jev’s VSM 2013 answers along the human Saudi–US difference by 87% of its size in English but only 62% in Arabic, with long-term orientation reversed; without a persona its answers resembled its American personas.
limitations: Hofstede references from unmatched samples.

subject: arxiv:2609.36965
headline: Language-specific open encoder ≈ hosted Jev in Chinese, better calibrated
claim_text: On CJ-Bench’s general subset, the open Chinese-Jev encoder reached 69.20% accuracy, 1.24% (relative) above hosted Jev, with ECE 3.78% against Jev’s 11.45%; across three specialised domains it reached 92% of Jev’s average accuracy at about 15 ms per decision.
limitations: Authors’ own benchmark.

subject: arxiv:2609.37470
headline: Two interfaces, same question: different decision on 32.8% of pairs
claim_text: Asking the same probability question through Jev’s Event and Choice interfaces changed the binary act/defer decision on 32.8% of valid pairs at a deferral cost of 0.10; disagreement between interfaces certified only 11–52% of mean pair error.
limitations: Synthetic worlds.

subject: arxiv:2609.37647
headline: Ahead of a 27B open LLM on 27/37 datasets; pooled Choice ECE 0.028
claim_text: On identical requests, Jev scored higher than Qwen3.8-27B on 27 of 37 datasets (11 with non-overlapping intervals; none of Qwen’s nine leads) and higher than Gemma-4-E4B on all 37; pooled over 22 Choice datasets and 279,925 answers its ECE was 0.028.
limitations: One frozen template per dataset; open models scored via exact option probabilities.

subject: arxiv:2609.37647
headline: Binary probabilities rank well; fixed 0.5 threshold does not
claim_text: Jev’s binary probabilities ranked well but were poorly placed against a fixed 0.5 threshold; thresholds tuned on training data raised UNFAIR-ToS micro-F1 from 0.50 to 0.75 and GoEmotions macro-F1 from 0.243 to 0.353.
limitations: Multi-label requests with rare labels.

subject: arxiv:2609.37647
headline: Calculation-heavy MMLU easier for Jev (94% vs 91%) — memorisation not ruled out
claim_text: Calculation-heavy MMLU subjects were easier for Jev than its other subjects (94.3% vs 91.3%), the reverse of both open models (Qwen 74.7% vs 83.0%); withholding the question dropped MMLU accuracy to 31.5%, which rules out shallow memorisation but not memorised question–answer pairs.
limitations: Long-established English benchmark; possible contamination.

subject: arxiv:2609.37832
headline: Cacheable scoring loses rule sensitivity (recall@1 1.00 → 0.24)
claim_text: Encoding candidates independently for caching cut rule-sensitive recall@1 from 1.00 to 0.24, while the joint scorer, which reads state, rules and candidate together, held 1.00 at a cost that grows with the menu; on real rules the joint scorer won 0.861 vs 0.500 on the short tier.
limitations: Small real-rule slices.

subject: arxiv:2609.38827
headline: ANLI: Neutral absorbs 51% of errors, at every position
claim_text: On ANLI, Jev 1.13 reached 74.95% accuracy but assigned 38.8% of all predictions and 51.3% of its 1,603 errors to Neutral, selecting Neutral 37.2–39.6% of the time at every candidate position.
metric: share of errors assigned to Neutral
limitations: One dataset for the motivating case.

subject: arxiv:2609.38827
headline: Ordinal scales compressed: decisions use 67–76% of gold support
claim_text: Across 36 ordinal datasets, final decisions used only 67–76% of the effective gold support against 87–102% on four nominal tasks; on fixed items with balanced support, utilisation fell as the scale was refined from 2 to 14 levels for every model.
limitations: Randomising candidate order weakens but does not remove the effect.

subject: arxiv:2609.38850
headline: Open RLCD: best selective prediction among SFT, STaR, GRPO
claim_text: An open RLCD recipe (calibrate, then reinforce) on Qwen3-1.7B matched or beat SFT, RFT/STaR and GRPO in accuracy and beat all of them in selective prediction on two reasoning tasks; with annotator-disagreement uncertainty it cannot beat cross-entropy.
limitations: Small model; three seeds.

subject: arxiv:2609.39111
headline: Open encoder–decoder: 78.05% on DecisionBench, 32 questions in 221 ms
claim_text: The open-weight Bongard model reached 78.05% accuracy over 23,900 DecisionBench decisions (fourth of 61 systems in the public comparison of 29 September 2026); on one RTX PRO 6000 its median latency was 36 ms for short requests and 221 ms for 32 questions about one state.
limitations: Rank depends on the leaderboard snapshot.; Latency measured on the authors’ own GPU.

subject: arxiv:2609.39496
headline: Present 99%, rejected when absent 7% — though Boolean checks get 99%
claim_text: On paired arithmetic problems with an explicit “None” option, Jev chose the correct value 99% of the time when it was present but correctly rejected only 7% of menus where it was absent; native Boolean verification rejected all three wrong candidates on 99% of the same answer-absent cases.
metric: correct rejection when the answer is absent
limitations: Synthetic arithmetic; hosted API only.

subject: arxiv:2609.39496
headline: Threshold from development data: rejection 7% → 79%
claim_text: A decision threshold selected on separate development problems raised correct rejection of answer-absent arithmetic menus from 7% to 79% while keeping 97% answer-present accuracy, without retraining or extra calls.
limitations: Threshold transfer beyond arithmetic not shown.

subject: arxiv:2609.40241
headline: Strong reranking quality; latency between local models and pointwise LLMs
claim_text: On hard candidate sets from three Amazon Reviews domains (2,580 users), Jev generally achieved higher NDCG@10 than SASRec, DCNv2 and Qwen2.5 rerankers on Video Games and Books; its observed latency grew much more slowly with set size than pointwise Qwen reranking but stayed well above the recommendation-specific models.
limitations: Hosted latency includes network overhead; local baselines run on one GPU.

subject: arxiv:2610.00213
headline: Population-scale reading audited by blind coders: sensitivity 0.999
claim_text: Reading 6,840 regex-flagged Texas crash narratives and 499,306 others, Jev confirmed 5,333 documenting a pregnant person; blind adjudication by two coders (Cohen’s κ 0.944) of a probability-stratified sample gave weighted sensitivity 0.999 and specificity 1.000, and the corrected estimate was 5,467 crashes (95% interval 5,306–5,577).
limitations: Same author team as other studies in this family.; Easy presence question on a pre-screened pool.

subject: arxiv:2610.00346
headline: Threshold for 5% risk still admits 31% of out-of-scope requests
claim_text: A threshold chosen on held-out data for 5% in-scope risk still let Jev accept 0.310 of out-of-scope requests on the 150-intent benchmark, and temperatures fitted on few options raised calibration error when many options were offered.
metric: out-of-scope acceptance at a 5% in-scope risk threshold
limitations: One intent benchmark.

subject: arxiv:2610.00346
headline: Yes/no swap flips half of the hosted model’s answers
claim_text: Swapping the meaning of yes and no against fixed rubrics flipped 50.5 of every 100 binary answers for hosted Jev, while fine-tuned open checkpoints cut their backbones’ flips on social-science items.
metric: answers flipped per hundred under a yes/no swap
limitations: Rubric-based binary tasks.

subject: arxiv:2610.00346
headline: Classifier first, Jev on escalation: same accuracy at 0.43 of the cost
claim_text: An intent-trained classifier as first stage, escalating uncertain inputs to Jev, matched Jev’s accuracy at 0.43 of its cost at full graphics-processor utilisation.
limitations: Cost depends on assumed GPU utilisation.

subject: arxiv:2610.00376
headline: Packet numbers in, 28% accuracy out — trees trained on 8k records reach 70%
claim_text: Given only the first ten packets’ sizes, directions and timings, Jev classified 9.80% of 52,000 QUIC flows correctly zero-shot (below a 22.79% majority constant) and 28.42% with 40 labelled examples; Random Forest and Extra Trees trained on 8,000 records reached 69.95% and 66.80% and beat Jev in every one of 26 weeks.
limitations: Unequal supervision budgets.

subject: arxiv:2610.00376
headline: 0.75 s vs 6.0 s per request; accuracy difference not established
claim_text: On a paired 100-record subset, Jev with 40 examples reached 29% accuracy at a median request time of 0.750 s against 37% and 6.036 s for GPT-5.6 Sol with high reasoning effort through Azure; the subset does not establish an accuracy advantage for either service.
limitations: 100 records; different service configurations.

subject: arxiv:2610.00381
headline: Same backbone, decision-native output: calibration error down up to 10×
claim_text: Against a generative baseline with the same backbone, data and schedule, the decision-distribution model cut calibration error by up to an order of magnitude and reliability error by up to two orders across medical imaging tasks, with comparable point predictions; counting was the exception.
limitations: Interface and training differences confounded.; Not clinical validation.

subject: arxiv:2610.00437
headline: Agent with spawned finite actions: Maze 0.96 vs 0.52
claim_text: With compositional action spawning, success rates reached 0.96 on Maze and 0.95 on Grid against 0.52 and 0.73 for FoldAgent, while end-to-end latency fell from the fastest baselines’ 47.91 and 61.44 s to 40.91 and 40.58 s; on LightsOut and 2048 higher scores came with longer runs.
limitations: Gains come from the whole policy, not only the scorer.

subject: arxiv:2610.00437
headline: Hosted Jev inside the agent: better on 3 of 8 tasks, 1.4–2.1× slower
claim_text: Swapping the finite scorer inside JevSpawn for hosted Jev improved PPNL, LightsOut (0.66 vs 0.61) and Sokoban, matched Maze and lowered Grid, RushHour, 2048 and Nullify, and took 1.4–2.1 times as long as local Qwen scoring across all eight tasks including API communication.
metric: time relative to local Qwen scoring
limitations: Hosted timing includes network round trips.

subject: arxiv:2610.00831
headline: Order flips on a third of 20-option items; rotation averaging halves them
claim_text: Across eleven open models, reversing the option list changed the argmax on 32.8% of banking20 and 33.4% of newsgroups items; averaging over cyclic rotations cut the order-flip rate to 0.14 and 0.18 and raised accuracy for 11 of 11 models on both tasks, at the cost of one prefill per rotation.
limitations: Open models only; hosted Jev not tested.

subject: arxiv:2610.01006
headline: Confidence ≠ knowing: +0.21–0.33 overconfidence past the knowledge boundary
claim_text: With no answer-relevant information Jev still assigned up to 0.80 to a salient option, and on news beyond an observed knowledge boundary its confidence exceeded accuracy by 0.21–0.33, a gap that recalibration on earlier months did not close.
metric: confidence minus accuracy beyond the knowledge boundary
limitations: Generated and curated interventions.

subject: arxiv:2610.01006
headline: Ask the model a targeted question instead of reading its confidence
claim_text: Asking targeted yes/no questions separated cases better than answer confidence: whether an outcome is settled reached AUROC 1.00 and whether evidence suffices 0.95 against 0.85 for confidence; asking whether Jev knows the answer reached 0.91 but lost its advantage with realistic names or dates removed.
limitations: Surface cues explain much of the knowledge-question signal.

subject: arxiv:2610.01079
headline: Intrusion pilot: F1 0.859, 4.8× faster than an LLM
claim_text: On a 300-flow NSL-KDD pilot (5,400 decisions), Jev reached F1 0.859 with one example per category, was 4.8 times faster and 3.8 times cheaper than GPT-5.6 Luna with 1.5 times higher novel-attack recall, and raised 15 times fewer false alarms than a Random Forest trained on the same examples.
limitations: Small pilot; historical dataset.

subject: arxiv:2610.01601
headline: Isolate candidates: order flips 18.2% → 1.2%
claim_text: Blocking attention between candidates and resetting their positions cut test permutation flip rates from 8.3% to 0.1% (Gemma 3 1B), 18.2% to 1.2% (Qwen3 1.7B) and 7.2% to 0.7% (Qwen3 4B) with competitive accuracy; isolation alone reduced flips to 3.82% and position reset alone made them worse (12.16%).
limitations: Open backbones only.

subject: arxiv:2610.01834
headline: Evaluates what is described; does not simulate what is not
claim_text: Jev solved 99% of Cognitive Reflection Test questions (95% interval 0.97–1.00) but in one-shot games chose as if a rational opponent acted at random; asked separately, it predicted the opponent’s action 90% of the time and played the best response 98% of the time once that action was stated (33% → 98%).
metric: accuracy when the opponent’s action is stated
limitations: Curated games and questions.

subject: arxiv:2610.01834
headline: Let code simulate: ALFWorld solved 31% → 87%
claim_text: In ALFWorld, Jev alone solved 31% of 134 games, favouring commands that mention objects named in the task; with a code-supplied lookahead it solved 87%, and with physics simulation from code it became an effective robot controller.
metric: ALFWorld games solved with code lookahead
limitations: Lookahead uses a copy of the environment.

subject: arxiv:2610.02046
headline: Semantic SQL: pruning + typed decisions finish 540K-pair joins
claim_text: JEVDB-Flash had the lowest latency on all 21 SemBench queries and the lowest cost on 19; on Shelob joins with up to 540K candidate pairs it finished every query at 95.7–97.5% mean F1, with Semantic Bloom Filters pruning 87.4% of pairs and condition-index scoring cutting reasoning-model escalations by 55.2%.
limitations: System gains mix pruning and model choice.

subject: arxiv:2610.02048
headline: Pre-registered gate: a third of SCADA reviews offloaded, accuracy kept
claim_text: In four sealed, pre-registered rounds, accepting only benign Jev verdicts confirmed by a rule tree spared an LLM reviewer 35–38% of windows with no loss of macro-F1, and the unchanged cascade stayed within the non-inferiority margin of its reviewer on two further networks.
metric: share of windows spared from LLM review
limitations: Simulated events.

subject: arxiv:2610.02048
headline: No labels needed: beats a supervised classifier on unseen subtypes
claim_text: Jev matched a hand-written rule tree in distribution (macro-F1 0.62–0.64 vs 0.56–0.61) and exceeded a supervised classifier by 0.36–0.42 macro-F1 on event subtypes absent from the classifier’s labels in all four rounds, outperforming it whenever fewer than about four labelled events per class were available.
limitations: Simulated events; prior correction needed.

subject: arxiv:2610.02076
headline: A frozen 4B LLM already matches community Jev-style models
claim_text: Without training, Qwen3.5-4B read through bracketed numeric identifiers resolved 188 of 231 public JevBench items (81.4%), matching or exceeding community Jev-style models on the same backbone (SemIf 186), and generating greedily picked the same candidate on all 231 items; LoRA with KL anchors raised it to 84.0% with ECE 0.050.
limitations: Small public item set.

subject: arxiv:2610.02267
headline: Hosted beats open on 9 of 11 harness decisions; routing at chance for both
claim_text: On byte-identical inputs, Jev was significantly more accurate than the open Laya on 9 of 11 agent-harness decision points (+10.8 to +46.0 pp); neither beat chance on zero-shot model routing, and Laya changed 30% of its answers when the option order was reversed and fell to 31% with 50 near-duplicate tools against 98% for Jev.
metric: decision points where Jev is significantly more accurate
limitations: Zero-shot, single versions.

subject: arxiv:2610.02267
headline: Self-audit: a 23.9% saving was really 4.3%
claim_text: Auditing its own pipeline, the study found that omitting the pre-screen cost turned a reported 23.9% saving into 4.3%, gate accuracy had been reported as end-to-end quality (58% vs 98%), and thresholds tuned in-sample for 5% misses gave up to 17% misses on held-out data.
metric: corrected saving after including pre-screen cost
limitations: Savings depend on unobserved production base rates.

subject: arxiv:2610.02267
headline: Hosted answers drift day to day (0.5%); open model reproduces exactly
claim_text: Repeating 1,080 decisions one day later changed 5 of Jev’s answers (0.5%), while the open Laya reproduced 1,180 of 1,180 decisions bit-for-bit on a second machine.
limitations: One-day interval.

subject: arxiv:2610.02293
headline: Turkish typed decisions: Jev fourth of 16 at a tenth of the leader’s time
claim_text: On HakemBench’s 16-row board, Gemini 3.8 Flash led with a composite of 0.888 and Jev 1.13 ranked fourth at 0.825 (0.811–0.837) with a median of 135 ms per item against 1,294 ms for the leader; the benchmark authors’ own model ranked seventh (0.660), and its numbers are flagged as not blind.
limitations: AI-made gold; authors also rank their own model.

subject: arxiv:2610.02486
headline: Open RLCD recipe trails plain cross-entropy by 2.5–3.0 points
claim_text: In a matched grid of heads and objectives on biomedical encoders, the released RLCD recipe of open System One models trailed cross-entropy by 2.5–3.0 points, mainly because its reward normalisation inflated the noisy score-function term 3.6–15-fold; an unbiased leave-one-out estimator recovered most of the gap, and after temperature scaling no objective was clearly better calibrated than cross-entropy.
metric: accuracy deficit of RLCD vs cross-entropy
limitations: One encoder for the objective grid.

subject: arxiv:2610.02586
headline: The label wins over the definition — and the cause is one rendering line
claim_text: In open typed-decision models the answer mostly followed option labels: deleting definitions left laya-td unchanged (0.8559 vs 0.8487), renaming options to A and B gained 0.151 accuracy, and one changed rendering line made laya exactly invariant while a contradicting label dropped von from 0.8511 to 0.2281.
metric: accuracy gain from neutral A/B names
limitations: Open-weight models only.

subject: arxiv:2610.03073
headline: Security-specialised 0.8B beats general 9B by 20.5 points
claim_text: Specialising Kev’s candidate scorer on 14 security tasks raised SecJev-0.8B’s task-macro accuracy by 39.40 points over Kev-0.8B and 20.51 points above general Kev-9B, with accuracy and latency close to answer-only generative fine-tuning at lower peak memory.
limitations: Specialised vs general comparison within one family.

subject: arxiv:2610.03324
headline: Definitions move 28% of answers — without reliably improving them
claim_text: Supplying a dataset’s hate-speech definition changed up to 28% of a decision model’s predictions but significantly improved agreement with annotations in only 29% of model–dataset comparisons and reduced it in as many; decomposing the definition into several questions helped in 20% and hurt in 37%.
metric: predictions changed by supplying a definition
limitations: Four datasets with different definitions.

subject: arxiv:2610.03324
headline: Within 1.6 macro-F1 of the best LLM at ~97% lower cost
claim_text: Commercial LLMs significantly outperformed all decision models on only one of four hate-speech datasets, and on a diagnostic set the best hosted decision model came within 1.6 macro-F1 points of the best commercial LLM at about 97% lower inference cost.
metric: macro-F1 gap to best commercial LLM
limitations: Cost comparison at list prices.

subject: arxiv:2610.03387
headline: Missing answer noticed 24.8% of the time (Jev) — Laya over-rejects
claim_text: With five TREC candidates and natural names, Jev detected only 24.8% of cases where the reference answer had been removed while falsely rejecting no present controls; Laya detected 97.2% but falsely rejected 69.7%; calibration-only thresholds moved Jev to 45.0% detection at 1.8% false rejection.
limitations: Small samples; four English tasks.

subject: arxiv:2610.03935
headline: Right mode, wrong mass: 89% placed where the truth is 36%
claim_text: On four-option items with analytically known distributions, Jev picked the most likely option on all 100 prior items and 67 posterior items, ahead of every non-thinking LLM, but placed 89.35% of the probability on the prior mode against 35.60% in the true distribution — the largest probability error of all configurations.
limitations: Synthetic probability tasks (100 items each).

subject: arxiv:2610.03935
headline: Near the number, rarely on it: 97% within ±1, 44% exact
claim_text: On tasks with a unique numerical answer, Jev landed within one of the exact value on 97% of repeating-division items but was exactly right on only 44% (39% on area inversion), while thinking LLMs recovered the exact values.
limitations: 100 items per task.

subject: arxiv:2610.03935
headline: Faster steps, slower agent: success 77.6% → 66.1%
claim_text: Replacing the action-selection step of a τ-bench tool agent with Jev cut median episode time from 267.1 s to 160.6 s but lowered success from 77.6% to 66.1% and raised the 95th-percentile time from 695.5 s to 816.0 s, as local decision errors accumulated over trajectories.
metric: τ-bench success with Jev action selection
limitations: One run per task; two environments.

subject: arxiv:2610.04345
headline: Wireless control: 3.5–8.5× faster than LLMs; quality depends on the task
claim_text: Jev cut median response latency by up to 8.5 times against generative LLMs in receive-antenna selection at a loss in decision quality to stronger task-specific methods, and matched the LLMs’ utility in intent-conditioned RAN slicing with more than 3.5 times lower median latency.
metric: median latency reduction vs LLMs (antenna selection)
limitations: Client-observed latency; simulated scenarios.

subject: arxiv:2610.04985
headline: Typed outputs, hijacked inputs: up to 100% injection success
claim_text: Text injected into the application state redirected Jev’s typed decisions: context-ignoring injection reached 96.5% attack success on support routing, and two Jev-specific injections, which claim the state is outdated and add false information, reached 100% on subscription cancellation and at least 96.8% on issue severity.
limitations: Author-built application tasks.

subject: arxiv:2610.04985
headline: Poisoned open checkpoints: >89% targeted redirection, clean accuracy intact
claim_text: Poisoning 5% of NanoJev’s training records with SFT or RLCD implanted backdoors that redirected over 89% of targeted inputs in most settings while clean accuracy stayed at 90.5–94.0%; RLCD generally gave higher attack success than SFT.
limitations: Open NanoJev; hosted model not poisoned.

subject: arxiv:2610.04985
headline: As a guard: ROC-AUC 0.95–1.0 on eight detection benchmarks
claim_text: Used as a detector, Jev reached ROC-AUC 0.95–1.0 on all eight prompt-injection, jailbreak, harmful-content and AI-text benchmarks, with calibrated accuracy of 87–99% on the six security benchmarks, while open NanoJev was near chance on several.
task: Injection, jailbreak, harmful-content and AI-text detection
limitations: Public benchmarks; thresholds calibrated per benchmark.

subject: arxiv:2610.05107
headline: Task-specialised open model beats Jev on rewriting, trails on routing
claim_text: On held-out search-decision datasets, both SearchJev models exceeded hosted Jev 1.13 on query rewriting and the 4B model also led on relevance, while Jev remained stronger on routing and verification; against same-size Qwen3.5 autoregressive models SearchJev decided 5.2–5.3 times faster with 41–74% lower average ECE.
metric: average ECE reduction vs same-size Qwen3.5
limitations: Authors’ benchmark and training data.

subject: arxiv:2610.05107
headline: Search agent: 3.7–4.7× faster, accuracy 45% → 54%
claim_text: In BrowseComp-Plus, dual-system agents that let SearchJev take confident short decisions cut median active search time 3.7–4.7-fold and output tokens 3.3–4.8-fold against a System-2-only agent while raising answer accuracy from 45% to up to 54%; against a Jev 1.13 agent the 0.8B model used fewer calls and less time at the same accuracy.
limitations: One deep-research benchmark.

subject: arxiv:2610.06354
headline: Reads every edge; counts degree right 68% of the time
claim_text: Jev answered every adjacency query correctly and performed relatively well on cycle, connectivity and distance judgments, but reached only 67.80% on exact degree and 61.25% on articulation points, so recognising an explicitly listed edge did not establish neighbour counting or connectivity reasoning.
limitations: Small graphs.

subject: arxiv:2610.06625
headline: Same accuracy, no cost advantage at batch prices
claim_text: Across seven political-science replications, Jev matched or came close to GPT-6 Luna and Qwen3.8-27B against human coding, but had no cost advantage over GPT-6 Luna at OpenAI’s batch prices: it bills the question and every option as input, 1.2–3.3 times as many input tokens per decision as Luna, which wrote about four output tokens per answer.
metric: input tokens billed relative to GPT-6 Luna
limitations: Prices at the time of study.

subject: arxiv:2610.06625
headline: Better calibrated than a commercial LLM, not than an open one
claim_text: When each question was asked once, Jev’s probabilities were better calibrated than GPT-6 Luna’s token probabilities but not consistently better than those of the open-weight Qwen3.8-27B.
limitations: Human coding as the benchmark.

subject: arxiv:2610.06744
headline: Order invariance by construction; sequential heads still flip 2–3%
claim_text: A head that scores each option blind to the others made the 182M-parameter Turkish model order-invariant by construction, whereas a sequential head trained with shuffled options changed 2.3–2.8% of its answers when only the option order changed; the released model answers in a median 102.5 ms on one CPU thread.
limitations: Same author built the benchmark; results not blind.

subject: src:typesafe-evals
headline: Vendor dashboard: 67.8% agreement at $0.0004 and 0.4 s per case
claim_text: The vendor’s workflow-evals dashboard averages four structured workflows (security incidents, agent-trace observability, invoice processing, customer service) against reference labels averaged from GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 at high thinking. In workflow mode it lists Jev at 67.8% mean agreement for $0.0004 and 0.4 s per case, against 74.1% for the best listed configuration (“sol”, $0.0836, 23.3 s) and 73.1% for Opus 5; every listed model scored higher in workflow mode than as a single prompt.
metric: mean agreement with reference labels (workflow mode)
limitations: Reference labels are frontier-model answers, not human gold.; Workflows written by the vendor.

subject: gh:anessbelbati/jev-rerank-bench
headline: Reranking: ties Cohere Rerank 4 Pro at half the latency
claim_text: Asked to rate thirty search results in one call, Jev’s four-level rubric scored nDCG@10 0.692 against 0.691 for Cohere Rerank 4 Pro when each dataset counts once (0.738 vs 0.756 when each question counts once) at 422 ms against 844 ms per query; on NevIR negation pairs Jev got 71% right against 67%.
limitations: Weighting questions equally puts Cohere ahead.

subject: gh:bitnovus/jev-spam-eval
headline: Zero-shot spam: matches a trained baseline; catches more new phishing
claim_text: With written category definitions and no labelled examples, Jev reached 98.64% accuracy on a 5,733-email ham/spam/phishing test against 98.87% for TF-IDF logistic regression trained on about 4,600 labelled messages per fold; on 853 recent phishing messages, Jev with enriched email context caught 95.31% against 75.26% for regression on the same evidence.
