limitations: Phishing recall comparison uses enriched context for both.

subject: gh:coldteadotai/abide
headline: Rule checks on agent edits: 10 of 39 flags confirmed
claim_text: Replaying 93 coding-agent sessions (1,256 edits, 147 turns) against the projects’ own rules, Jev flagged 39 edits and 15 turns as rule violations; an independent reviewer confirmed 10 of the edits and 11 of the turns.
metric: flagged edits confirmed by a reviewer
limitations: Two repositories; one reviewer.

subject: gh:gaurav-gosain/jev-sec-bench
headline: Blind security run: 96.5% on prompt injection, 89% on code pairs
claim_text: Run once against jev-1.13.0 without threshold tuning, Jev classified all 662 labelled messages of deepset/prompt-injections with 96.5% accuracy (F1 95.6%), and scored the vulnerable half above its secure twin in 178 of 200 matched code pairs (89.0%).
limitations: Public corpora; possible training overlap unknown.

subject: gh:gautamtalksdev/jevbench
headline: Overconfident where 100 annotators disagree (0.81 vs 0.47)
claim_text: In a preregistered ChaosNLI study, Jev’s Choice probabilities were close to calibrated where annotators agreed but overconfident where they split (mean confidence 0.81 against 0.47 annotator agreement; bias-corrected ΔECE 0.264); normalised Noul probabilities degraded less (ΔECE 0.076).
limitations: One dataset; Choice and Noul arms differ.

subject: gh:jevals/jevals-data
headline: Independent boards: top tier on yes/no, second on intents, no model beats guessing on helpfulness
claim_text: In the 2026-09-18 release scored against human labels, Jev tied Gemini 3.8 Flash for first in Decision Score on PubMedQA yes/no questions (69.0 vs 73.0) at $0.029 per 1,000 decisions, tied for second of eight on Banking77 intents (67.8 vs 74.1), and like every model did not clearly beat guessing on HelpSteer2 helpfulness.
metric: Decision Score on PubMedQA (100 = perfect, 0 = base-rate guessing)
limitations: Three tasks; leaderboard ranks use interval ties.

subject: gh:lexmount/webjev
headline: Browser tasks: specialised open model 38.5% vs Jev 16.7%; single steps alike
claim_text: Driving the same jev-ultrafast browser agent on 125 real-website tasks graded by deterministic verifiers, WebJev-35B-A3B completed 38.52% and Jev 1.13 16.67%, although on eight single-step decision benchmarks the two were close (83.72% vs 84.70%).
limitations: Authors’ task suite; their own model is the comparator.

subject: gh:nanmicoder/jev-arena
headline: 10,000 comments: 4× faster than a chat model, five points less agreement
claim_text: On 10,000 comments re-labelled by GPT-6 Astra, Jev 1.13 finished in 203.2 s for $0.84 against 823.5 s and an estimated $1.50 for DeepSeek Flash, with lower agreement on all three labels (all three right: 62.69% vs 67.26%).
metric: all three labels agree with the reference
limitations: Reference labels from another model, not human gold.

subject: gh:realzachi/pg-jev
headline: More rows per request, fewer correct: 100% → 77–94%
claim_text: Packing rows into one Jev request, where Jev must find each row by its position in an array, the author found batches of 1–20 rows judged 100% correctly against ground truth on three conditions over 400-row tables, batches of 40 at 92–98% and batches of 80 at 77–94%; batches of 20 cost 4% more tokens than batches of 40 at about the same latency.
metric: rows judged correctly in batches of 80
limitations: Three structured conditions; author-run.

subject: gh:shimo4228/jev-skill-router
headline: A week as a skill router: 28 of 539 suggestions used, then removed
claim_text: Run for a week as a Claude Code skill router, Jev’s suggestion was followed by a call of the suggested skill in 28 of 539 cases; the author removed it because the log could not separate Jev’s picks from the agent’s own choices.
metric: suggestions followed by the suggested skill
task: Skill routing in a coding agent
limitations: One user’s week of sessions.

subject: gh:suenot/codex-jev-router
headline: Routing subagents with Jev: cheaper than one baseline, dearer than another
claim_text: In the author’s four-arm benchmark, Codex subagents whose model was chosen by Jev were 27.2% cheaper than fixed high-effort subagents yet 69.7% more expensive than a single extra-high-effort agent, and the router was withdrawn.
metric: cost relative to a single extra-high-effort agent
limitations: Author-run tasks; the comparison depends on the baseline chosen.

subject: gh:uspraveen/jevify
headline: Open 9B readout edges Jev on accuracy and calibration in the author’s benchmark
claim_text: On the author’s jev-bench, Jev 1.13.0 reached 0.733 accuracy with ECE 0.113 — calibrated on crisp questions, overconfident where people disagree — while a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-9B readout with a coherence objective reached 0.763 accuracy, ECE 0.056 and a distance to the human label distribution of 0.301 against Jev’s 0.432.
limitations: The author built the benchmark and the winning model.

subject: gh:wondertwins/jev-benchmark
headline: Chess: random from the raw board, competent once code supplies the facts
claim_text: Choosing chess moves, jev-1.13.0 was no better than random from a raw board (mean centipawn loss 533 from a FEN string against 403 for random moves) but fell to 144 with code-computed facts; with one-ply tactical facts it found mate-in-one 24% of the time and played at roughly 950 Elo.
metric: mean centipawn loss with code-computed facts
limitations: Single author; one engine-anchored ladder.

subject: gh:yinsongxu/llm2jev
headline: Local 4B readout: 76% on public JevBench at 48 ms
claim_text: On the 231 public JevBench items, LLM2Jev on a local Qwen3.5-4B reached 76.2% accuracy with a median latency of 48 ms (P95 346 ms), against 652 ms (P95 722 ms) for hosted Jev 1.13.0.
limitations: Hosted latency includes the network; local runs do not.

subject: gh:zhuyansen/jev-search-rerank-eval
headline: Grading Jev with Jev’s own labels inflates its gain
claim_text: Reranking an embedding ranker’s top 30 with Jev changed NDCG@10 by +0.053 under Jev-made labels, +0.012 under merged labels and −0.028 under labels from an unrelated model, while fusing Jev with the embedding ranking gained +0.090 and survived removing Jev from the judging.
metric: NDCG@10 change from Jev reranking (unrelated-model labels)
limitations: One catalogue; graded labels from model judges.
